usageNotes: Use this endpoint to discover valid CPU model names before creating or reconfiguring a VM — the returned `name` values are the identifiers accepted by the `cpu` parameter in VM create/update calls. Custom models are visibility-filtered by the caller's Mapping.{Audit,Use,Modify} privilege on `/mapping/cpu/<name>`, so the list may vary between users. When targeting an ARM guest, pass `arch=aarch64`; omitting `arch` defaults to the host's native architecture.

examples.summary: List all available QEMU CPU models on node pve1 for x86_64 guests

tips: Models with `abstract: true` (e.g. x86-64-v2, x86-64-v3) are PVE baseline profiles — they cannot be used as the `reported-model` field when defining a custom CPU type.
Custom CPU models appear with a `custom-` prefix in their `name`; these are defined via the `/cluster/mapping/cpu` API and stored cluster-wide.

Running this against any online node in the cluster is sufficient — the built-in model list is QEMU-version-dependent, so results may differ if nodes run different QEMU versions after a partial upgrade.
